title: Bramm Yards redevelopment plan and digital billboard
subtitle: Also covered: a Victoria Street digital sign, 2025 budget timelines and a Dundee North plan purchase order increase.
overview: The Finance and Corporate Services Committee made recommendations on four main items. The biggest was the Bramm Yards, a large city-owned site near downtown. The committee recommended approving a revised vision, setting aside reserve money for pre-design studies, and starting a public search for a master developer, with extra direction on market timing, RFP rating criteria and University of Waterloo involvement {{vote:m5}}.

The committee also recommended allowing a digital billboard at 1495 Victoria Street North, against staff advice, with limits on brightness, size and operating hours {{vote:m4}}. For the budget, it recommended approving the 2025 timelines and shortening the period for Council to amend the Mayor's proposed budget {{vote:m3}}. It recommended a purchase order increase for the Dundee North Secondary Plan {{vote:m2}}.

These are recommendations only. Council must adopt them, and Council will get more information on Bramm Yards RFP rating criteria on June 24, 2024. For residents, the decisions affect how a major public site is developed, how bright a roadside sign can be, and when budget decisions are finalized.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended approving the revised vision and development principles, allocating up to $400,000 from the Environmental Remediation Reserve for pre-design reports, and authorizing a public RFP for a master developer.

decisions.item: Bramm Yards market assessment and RFP criteria
decisions.detail: The committee recommended that staff do a market assessment on timing and development limits, involve the University of Waterloo in it, and report on RFP rating criteria at the June 24, 2024 Council meeting.

decisions.item: Digital billboard at 1495 Victoria Street North
decisions.detail: The committee recommended approving the sign amendment, despite a staff recommendation to refuse, with brightness limits, an overnight shutoff from midnight to 6 a.m., a 5.0 metre setback and a maximum sign area of 20.24 square metres.
The committee recommended approving the 2025 budget timelines and shortening the 30-day period for amending the Mayor's proposed budget to end with the December 12, 2024 meeting.

decisions.item: Dundee North Secondary Plan purchase order
decisions.detail: The committee recommended increasing Purchase Order 213285 by $150,000 plus HST of $19,500, for a total of $169,500.

debate: On the billboard, staff recommended refusal. They said it conflicts with the vision for low-rise commercial corridors, that the multi-use trail has changed who uses the street, and that approval could set a precedent. The applicant's representatives said it replaces a larger, older sign and reduces advertising area.

Councillors who supported the billboard said it would be smaller and better controlled than the existing sign. They also said the approval is site-specific, Council has the final say on any future requests, and local businesses could benefit. Some raised concern about too many billboards.

On overnight hours, the applicant had offered a blackout from 11 p.m. to 6 a.m. Council chose midnight to 6 a.m. so it could be revisited later more easily than a stricter rule could be loosened. Staff said any hours must be written into the sign by-law to be enforceable.

On Bramm Yards, councillors asked about the contamination risk and the choice to sell rather than lease. Staff said a sale suits a project of this scale and that conditions in the purchase agreement can protect the vision. A councillor worried that asking for a single master developer could limit bidders. Staff said they could revisit the approach.

Councillors differed on how much to add to the RFP. One wanted Council to see the rating criteria first, and another asked to delay the RFP until environmental and market work was done. Staff said those studies would come first anyway, and that sale proceeds fund the economic development investment fund and affordable housing, so adding requirements could reduce proceeds.
